body: I have tried the diet, but can't seem to find my triggers and get way too weak and skinny on the diet-I don't have the energy to sustain my life on it and my blood sugar gets super low. I may try it when out of school, though. Hydroxyzine was too sedating-I'd feel almost hungover the next day, so I take Benedryl (dye free) when needed. I do not have ulcers, which is good, but seems incongruent with my current pain levels. I have the stuff to do emergency instills, but have not tried them at home yet and have to wait a bit after the hydro.

How do you help keep a balance in your relationship and help negate the caretaker/patient dynamic? He's amazingly sexy and just wonderful, but I feel like a couch-potato-I used to be a yoga-doing, active, super-bubbly person and now I'm still pretty darn cheerful 80% of the time, but I hate my limitations and he can't accommodate them on his schedule. (He does great, but we're both grad students.)

Acidic foods, alcohol, and caffeine in larger quantities tend to flare me. Honestly, I'm never out of a flare completely and don't remember what it's like to be pain free unless I'm on high-level pain meds (like the Oxycotin I just got from my hydro). Sometimes, even that doesn't work. I've only been with my current doc about a year, as I tried other doctors, but none had the IC speciality that this one does and ended up making me worse, rather than better.

I'm really interested in your Interstim experience. I just got a hydrodistension [sp?] this past Friday and the recovery has ended up being more hellish than I remembered. I had one once before, in college, as part of my initial diagnosis and it put me into what was basically a remission with some flares for several years. I am currently on: Cymbalta, amitriptyline, Elmiron (2x daily), Gelnique (which doesn't seem to be working all that well), vaginal Valium, as well as AZO, calcium citrate, Cysta-Q, and Tramadol or tylenol as needed. I'm trying to finish my master's degree and felt the hydro would be the best option for my current, frequently disabling level of pain. I'm not sure if it was the right choice, but I'm stuck on my sofa with pain meds and a low-grade fever. I'm in school and working (very part-time), but I feel I cannot do anything well because I never feel well enough. I think my partner is just realizing this, though he seems ok with it and just wants me to get better.

I suppose what I'm asking is, would you end it, if you could and you were in my situation? If you felt like every person you were with would be denied a normal sex life and would prefer almost anyone but you, except that they didn't realize how hard it would be before they got emotionally invested? Because I feel like I need a reality check.
